title: Draw and fact-check a sticker for every bird species
summary: Huashu used an AI pipeline to draw stickers for all 11,064 living bird species, reporting 7,676 passed an automated field-mark review after rounds of redraws.
agent_role: The pipeline found reference photos, drew each sticker, upscaled and cut it out, then a separate AI reviewer scored it and triggered redraws; the human set the quality bar and invites birder corrections.
outcome: Author reports 7,676 of 11,064 stickers meet the quality bar; 3,388 fall short and the best-scoring version was kept.
what_they_did: Huashu, who makes a bird-watching app, built a sticker for every living bird species. For each, the pipeline picked a reference photo, drew the bird with GPT-image, upscaled it and cut it out. A separate AI reviewer scored each sticker on bill, eyes, legs and plumage against the photo. Low scorers were redrawn.
how_it_went: The author reports 11,064 stickers in total, with names in up to 43 languages. 7,676 pass the bar; in the last round 211 of 852 borderline stickers failed a second blind review and were redrawn.
worth_knowing: The author says these are friendly illustrations, not field-guide plates, and to check a field guide for fine details. Many reference photos carry non-commercial or unrecorded licenses.
prompt: Help me make a matching set of illustrated stickers for [list of species or items]. For each one, find an openly licensed reference photo and record its source and license. Draw a sticker in [style] with a white outline, then compare it against the photo on [key features to check] and give it a score out of 100. Redraw anything below [score] up to [number] times and keep the best version. Show me the first five results and the scoring notes before running the full list.

curation.rationale: A large, well-documented AI pipeline that drew, scored and redrew stickers for all 11,064 bird species with open data and honest quality numbers; the exact agent tooling is only implied by repo tags.
